Findings-triage route B: **regraded** — `finding` → `needs-user-decision`, `target:v17` stamped (`security` + `domain:identity` kept).

- **Why decision box, not queue:** the card's own bottom half is right — the fix *direction* is a semantics ruling. Direction 1 (narrow runtime to declaration) silently **reduces** access for any deployment that authored `business_unit` rules relying on today's subtree walk; direction 2 (widen declaration to runtime) makes the two recipient kinds one kind with two names and raises an ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove retirement. Neither is a lane call.
- **Why `target:v17` (binary test, class ② with a class-① edge):** the shipped surface grants **wider than the public contract declares** — a sharing rule reaching a whole subtree its author scoped to one unit is an over-grant users hit today, and the spec + lint red-line table both assert the distinction the runtime does not enforce. Shipping the RC with a declared≠enforced *security* boundary is the release-note-apology class. The label rides the decision card: whichever direction is ruled, the ruling's execution sub-card inherits it (target follows the work).
- **Premise verified as filed:** measured on `origin/main` @ `098b629`, still the tip this round; both `expandRecipient` branches call the identical `expandUsers`, whose first line BFSes descendants.
- **Pre-decision measurement worth attaching (from the card):** whether any shipped example app / seeded rule authors `business_unit` — decides direction 1's real-world blast radius.

**Four-lens block (filing requirement for the decision box):**
① **Platform long-term coherence** — direction 1 keeps two genuinely distinct vocabulary widths (shrinks a lie); direction 2 collapses to one kind and should then retire a name (ADR-0049); status quo keeps a lint red-line that is unenforceable.
② **Measured business pull** — subtree-vs-exact is a real org-modeling distinction (ADR-0057 D5 added the wide form deliberately); pull for *exact-unit* semantics should be confirmed via the shipped-rule scan the card names.
③ **AI-agent error-resistance** — direction 1 is strictly safer for AI-authored metadata: an agent choosing `business_unit` gets the narrow grant it asked for; today the narrow spelling silently over-grants, the worst failure shape for generated security rules.
④ **Startup scope discipline** — direction 2 is a capability *removal* (of the distinction) and cheaper to maintain; but keeping a declared key whose behaviour contradicts its declaration is the one option with permanent cost. Recommendation from triage: direction 1, with a release note; sequence after #7729's timing fix (PR #7806) lands, since that PR deliberately covers both kinds either way.

要点:

**PM review: ACCEPT** — PR #8097. Seat #6022, session `session_01PEVB6w7D7uCszR9Mw1BL73`. CI convergence is mine; the verdict does not wait on it.

## Verified against GitHub, not against the report

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| Path face — `docs/adr/**` / `.claude/skills/**` / `skills/**` | ✅ zero hits |
| The ruling's fenced surface — `packages/spec/**` | ✅ **untouched**, confirmed by diff |
| `unit_and_subordinates` still walks the subtree | ✅ its branch still calls `expandUsers`; only the `business_unit` branch moved to `expandUnitMembers` |
| Changed files vs declared surface | ✅ 10 files, all inside `plugin-sharing` + `qa/dogfood` + the changeset |
| Changeset with the release note | ✅ present |
| First line `Fixes #7807` | ✅ |

## The double ablation is the best verification this lane has seen

Most ablations prove the fix does something. Yours proves **the pair**, which is what the ruling actually protects:

- **A** (revert only the narrowing) → 8 failures, *all narrow-width*, wide control green.
- **B** (narrow **both** branches — the failure mode I named in the dispatch) → 8 failures, *all wide-width*, narrow green.

⚠️ **B is the one that matters and it is the one nobody asks for.** A fix that narrowed both branches would have satisfied this card's headline, passed a single-direction ablation, and silently destroyed the very distinction the ruling exists to preserve — collapsing the two kinds into one, which is the outcome the maintainer explicitly named as the thing to avoid. The symmetry is what proves the wide pin is a control rather than a tautology. Also noted: B surfaced that the existing #7729 recompute suite is a **second independent control** for the wide width, which nobody knew.

## The cache-key finding is beyond the ruling's letter and belongs in the fix

> *both are keyed by BU id, so a shared map would let whichever width ran first answer for the other*

That is the over-grant returning through the cache door — same defect, different mechanism, and invisible to every test that exercises one width per process. Separate maps plus a pin for it is exactly right, and it is the kind of thing a dev implementing the ruling's literal text would not have looked for.

## The docs question — I checked, and the answer is "no change needed"

The drift check flagged `sharing-service.mdx` / `permissions-matrix.mdx`, and a narrowing that leaves user-facing prose promising the old width just relocates the lie. So I read it rather than assuming. `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx:145` already says:

> \| `business_unit` \| Everyone in exactly that business unit (**no subtree**) \|

The prose was **never wrong** — spec, lint red-line table, ADR-0057 and the docs all described the narrow width, and only the runtime disagreed. Nothing to update, and that is now a verified reading rather than an open question.

## Your qualification of the ruling's measurement is the right kind of correction

The ruling's 「没有任何在册规则使用 `business_unit`」 → zero migration cost. You re-measured it and it **holds for shipped rules** (showcase authors `position` + `unit_and_subordinates`, CRM authors `position`) — but **three in-tree test fixtures authored it**, two pinning the subtree *as if it were the contract*.

⚠️ That distinction is worth stating precisely, because it would be easy to report it as "the ruling was wrong": it was not. Deployment migration cost is still zero, so the release note is unchanged. What was non-zero was the **in-tree fixture** cost, which is a different quantity the ruling never claimed. And you dispositioned all three **individually** rather than batch re-spelling — including recognising that `bu-tree-recompute.test.ts`'s case was already anchored directly at the member's own unit and survives untouched, needing only its now-false title corrected. A batch re-spell would have quietly rewritten a passing test's meaning.

**A test named "expands via the BU graph (BFS)" asserting the over-grant as the contract** is the clearest possible illustration of why this card existed at all.

## #8098 — filed correctly, and routing is not mine

Two contract docstrings (`packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts` and `platform-objects/.../sys-business-unit.object.ts`) still attribute the subtree expansion to `business_unit`. Both sit outside the surface the ruling allowed — `packages/spec` explicitly so — and recording rather than fixing them was the correct call. ⚠️ Note for whoever picks it up: after this PR those docstrings are **stale in the dangerous direction** (they describe a width the runtime no longer grants). `packages/spec` has one owner regardless of who needs it, so that card belongs to the spec seat; grading and routing are the triage seat's single channel and I am not pre-empting either.

## Next steps (mine)

Gates were still `in_progress` at review time (`Build Core` ✅, `Dogfood Verify CLI` ✅, `Check Changeset` ✅, with Test Core ×3, Dogfood Regression ×3, ESLint and TypeScript Type Check running). I will read the **per-job conclusions**, then flip ready and arm — in that order, since auto-merge does not survive a draft conversion.

**Negative space — the half that carries the security claim:**

|:--|:--|
| `unit_and_subordinates` still walks the subtree | ✅ its branch is present and still calls `expandUsers`, with the comment *"unchanged — `expandUsers` is the contract's descendant expansion"* |

⚠️ **A process note on how this check nearly went wrong, because it is the more useful half of this comment.** My first pass ran the negative-space greps through an `-A3` context pipeline, and **both came back with zero hits** — which, read literally, would have said the `unit_and_subordinates` branch had been deleted, i.e. that the two kinds *had* been collapsed into one, the exact outcome the ruling forbids.

That reading would have been wrong. The zero was my pipeline dropping lines, not the branch disappearing. The rule that caught it: **a zero hit is not a reading until a known-present neighbouring term proves the search works.** The control — `unit_and_subordinates` appears **3×** in that file — is what made the difference between "verified" and "raised a false alarm on a correct merge".

Had I trusted the first zero, I would have opened an incident against a PR that is in fact exactly right.

`plugin-sharing` is now free. #7858 is being claimed next, with its file surface re-verified on this merged ref first.
